subject: Food Science
title: pH and Acidity
description: A quick win: understand pH and Acidity.

hook.text: Lemon juice has a pH of 2. Egg whites sit at 9. That difference changes everything about how food behaves.

buildup.text: pH measures hydrogen ion concentration on a 0–14 scale. Below 7 is acidic, above 7 is alkaline.

discovery.text: Acid denatures proteins—that's why ceviche 'cooks' raw fish without heat. Lime juice unfolds the proteins.

twist.text: Most bacteria can't survive below pH 4.6. That's why pickles, vinegar, and fermented foods last so long.

climax.text: Bakers add baking soda (alkaline) to cookie dough to trigger browning. pH controls color and flavor.

punchline.text: Sour or bitter, safe or spoiled—pH decides.

quiz.question: Why does ceviche 'cook' raw fish without heat?
options: Acid from lime juice denatures the proteins
